author: Claude (independent verification track)
candidate: PORT OCCUPANCY / LEGAL E^1 PHASE REPAIR
scope: Q2 / Area-A. Residual states fetched by their Round-80 (root, idx) provenance directly out of the stored checkpoint frontiers -- a lookup of preserved data, not a frontier replay; nothing expanded, searched or re-generated. No continuation solver built.

definitions.E2: macro edge (ell=5, w3:120); orbit-preserving, phase +2, costs one Ndef -- affordable since every residual state has Ndef=0 (verified)
definitions.legality: both need a full five-step rotation run, legal exactly when the current hexagon holds only the endpoint, and both need their joint target unvisited. Taken from the engine itself via macro.rotation_runs + exact.extend, not inferred from orbit identity.
definitions.PhaseClosure: positions of q0 reachable from the endpoint by any sequence of orbit-preserving macro edges. Until the walk leaves q0 these are its only moves, so the first orbit-changing edge of any continuation departs from this set.
definitions.NEXT_pinned: cover-candidate orbits openable by one macro edge from PhaseClosure(s). DIAGNOSTIC ONLY -- closing on it would be unsound, since the walk may re-enter another open orbit first and open from there.
definitions.NEXT_sound: the above plus everything openable from any already-open orbit reachable through open orbits, arrival phase over-approximated to all five. Only this may close a state.
definitions.cover_compatibility: exact: force q into the cover and re-decide the Round-79 instance on U minus block(q) with K-1 blocks and slack b - waste(q)

stage_A_e1_closure_census.round_77_cross_check: maximal consecutive E1 chain is 4, exactly as Round 77 observed; the Area-A prune never blocks an E1 step here, the two histograms are identical
stage_A_e1_closure_census.e2_matters: 448 states have PhaseClosure size 1 while 493 have E1-chain 0, so 45 states have E1 blocked but E2 available

stage_C_e1_depletion: NOT ATTEMPTED -- the brief's payoff gate stops the round when B closes 0

headroom_ceiling.measurement: how many states WOULD close under deliberately unsound strengthenings, bounding everything this direction could ever deliver
headroom_ceiling.interpretation: even forbidding ALL phase repair -- assuming away E1 and E2 entirely, which is false -- the first-open test closes only 13 of 6,657 (0.20%). Allowing the true phase closure drops that to 1. So E1 costs this direction 12 states; the direction was worth at most 13 to begin with.

structural_reason_for_zero_payoff.not_E1: E1 is not the bottleneck here. Port occupancy genuinely pins the phase in 448 states and caps NEXT_pinned at 4-54 against a candidate family of about 130 -- a real restriction. It simply does not matter.
structural_reason_for_zero_payoff.the_actual_cause: a first-open test can only close a state when EVERY orbit it can open is cover-incompatible. Round 81 measured that the median state has 128 of 144 orbits individually cover-compatible, because SLACK-COVER constrains which K-subsets work, not which single orbits are usable. With about 90% of all orbits individually usable, and 1-17 openable even from a single pinned phase, at least one is cover-compatible in 6,644 of 6,657 states.
structural_reason_for_zero_payoff.conclusion: first-open tests are exhausted at every refinement level -- orbit (Round 81) and (orbit,phase)+occupancy (this round). The measured ceiling for the whole family is 13 states.

what_would_be_needed_next: a condition on a SEQUENCE or a SET rather than the next single step: the cover is a set constraint and only a set/sequence constraint can interact with it

the leak in NEXT_sound is re-entry into another open orbit with the arrival phase over-approximated to all five; the arrival phase is actually determined by the entering joint, so a phase-exact multi-step relation is possible -- but that is the phase-level continuation solver the brief defers
